text:
maria: Quick sync — we need to finalize SLOs and graceful-degrade modes for Hosted API PRD. Customer asks (FinReg Co) require SLA negotiation. Draft PRD: https://redwood.docs/prd/slo-fallbacks (WIP)

sam: +1. main tradeoff is cost vs tail latency. Proposal: two-tier SLOs: standard (p95 <= 150ms, error rate <= 0.5%) and premium (p95 <= 80ms, error rate <= 0.2%).

liam: For error budget burn, we should map routes -> budgets. critical routes (chat/stream) get dedicated buffer. Also need clear rollout canary: `canary=5% traffic -> monitor 30m`

anya: FinReg will insist on 99.9% uptime SLA on premium. Need fallback plan when budget exhausted.

maria: Fallbacks we discussed: 1) route to compatible smaller model (latency reduces but quality drops) 2) degrade features (disable long-context or embeddings) 3) switch to queued mode (longer latency but preserve correctness). Which combination is acceptable?

kevin: For product acceptance criteria, proposal:
```
- SLOs defined per-route in PRD
- Automatic fallback triggers when 10% error budget burned in 1h
- Canary rollout plan + runbook
- Telemetry: per-token cost, p50/p95/p99, error-rate, fallback-events
```

jules: Can we quantify quality impact of model fallback? need evals for top 10 customer prompts.

sam: Agree. Add acceptance criterion: "fallback quality regression <= 5% on customer eval set". We'll need eval harness and perf numbers.

liam: Ops: runbook for fallback should include automatic alert (pager) when fallback engaged > 2m AND postmortem template auto-created.

anya: Also add communication plan for customers (onboarding + incident notifications). FinReg needs audit trail.

maria: Ok. Action items:
- sam: add concrete SLO numbers to PRD + model variants mapping (due EOD Thu)
- jules: run evals for fallback quality (due next Tue)
- liam: draft runbook + alerting thresholds (due Fri)
- kevin: update acceptance criteria and customer comms (due Mon)

kevin: One more question — how strict should SLO rollback be? if canary fails, do we rollback entirely or reduce to 50%? prefer staged rollback.

sam: staged rollback policy in PRD: canary -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> abort. Each step requires 30m watch and manual approval except abort.

maria: Sounds good. I'll consolidate and post PRD update later today. Thanks all :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy started: canary/slo-fallbacks v1.3 to prod (5%)

liam: Noted, monitoring hooks live. ping if you see increased fallback-events.

maria: Closing thread here — we'll reconvene after the canary results. Thanks."
